method.ws: Point-in-polygon lookup of each representative site in the Aqueduct 4.0 baseline_annual GDB layer; value = bws_score (0-5) / 5; mean of points where two sites listed.
method.wue: Preference order: site/region-specific operator disclosure (AWS regional fact sheets 2025, Microsoft location fact sheets/Li et al. compilation) > national regulator statistic > operator fleet average > peer-reviewed climate model; null if none.

fab_water.metric: Water withdrawal per unit electricity, TSMC corporate (Taiwan fabs + subsidiaries)
fab_water.source: TSMC 2025 Annual Report, Ch.7 (Corporate Social Responsibility): 'TSMC Water Usage in Recent Two Years' table (Total Water Usage, million m3; Note 1: Taiwan fabs and subsidiaries, city water + reclaimed water) and 'Used 5,780 GWh in renewable energy ... renewable energy use to 20.1%'. 2023 figures from TSMC 2024 Annual Report p.159.
fab_water.note: Derived by me: 151e9 L / (5,780 GWh / 0.201 = ~28,756 GWh) = ~5.25 L/kWh. 'Water usage' is intake (withdrawal-like: city + reclaimed water), not consumption; much of it returns as treated wastewater. This is ~20x a typical temperate data-center WUE and ~2-3x even Singapore DC WUE. Per-wafer intensity (153 L per 12-inch-equivalent wafer mask layer) is the more physical basis if the model tracks wafer output.

fab_water.metric: Water usage per unit energy, TSMC corporate
fab_water.unit: L/kWh (total water usage / total energy incl. natural gas & diesel)
fab_water.source: Water: TSMC 2024 Annual Report p.159 ('Total Water Usage' 129 million m3). Energy: TSMC 2024 Sustainability Report (total energy 27,456 GWh; purchased electricity ~93.0%, natural gas 6.9%, diesel 0.1%).
fab_water.note: Derived by me: 129e9 L / 27,456e6 kWh = 4.70 L/kWh of total energy; ~5.05 L/kWh per kWh of purchased electricity (x/0.93). The 27,456 GWh figure was taken from search-result excerpts of the 2024 Sustainability Report (the PDF at https://esg.tsmc.com/en-US/file/public/2024-TSMC-Sustainability-Report-e.pdf blocked automated download) - verify before relying on it. Consistent with the 2025 derivation (~5 L/kWh).

caveats: Water stress values are Aqueduct 4.0 BASIN-level scores at the site point (HydroBASINS level 6 sub-basin), normalized score/5 with all-sector weighting; state/province and country scores are given in each note. Basin and state values can differ a lot (e.g. Ashburn basin 0.16 vs Virginia state 2.56; San Francisco basin 1.76 vs California 4.03; Mumbai basin 1.37 vs Maharashtra 4.20). Pick one scope consistently.

Aqueduct measures physical withdrawal/renewable supply. It does not capture import-dependent supply (Singapore), desalination (Riyadh) or reservoir-drought risk (Taiwan 2021). Singapore's basin value 0 is misleading for policy purposes.

WUE values mix scopes and definitions: Microsoft = cooling + humidification water per IT kWh; AWS = water withdrawn per IT kWh; IMDA = national median of large DCs; GDS = fleet average (denominator not stated). All are ON-SITE only and exclude water consumed in electricity generation (off-site/indirect WUE, often 1-4 L/kWh), which the app's W = E * WUE does not include.
The app multiplies WUE (per IT kWh) by E (annual FACILITY energy). Strictly, W = (E / PUE) * WUE. Using facility energy overstates water by the PUE factor (~1.1-1.4x).
Hyperscaler regional WUE swings a lot year to year (e.g. AWS Frankfurt 0.01 -> 0.17; Microsoft APAC 0.03 -> 0.25). Prefer multi-year means for stable modeling.
Several values are DESIGN targets for sites not yet operating (Taiwan 1.00, Mexico 0.056; Microsoft India 0.00 noted but not used), flagged confidence 'projected'.

The app applies data-center WUE to ALL site types. That is wrong for fabs and mines. Fabs: TSMC's intake is about 5 L per kWh of electricity (see fab_water), roughly 20x typical DC WUE, driven by ultrapure-water production, not cooling. Mines (Greenbushes lithium, Grasberg copper/gold, Spruce Pine quartz) use water mainly for ore processing, dust suppression and tailings, which scale with ore tonnage, not electricity. They need a per-tonne water intensity from the operators' sustainability reports, not a WUE.
Saudi Arabia (sa) WUE is null: no credible disclosure found. The task mentions 28 regions but 25 region IDs were listed; all 25 are covered.
